# 1.2.59 - what a player writes stays words

The third stage on the way to 1.3.0, and a security one. Several things a
player can type - or send from the browser console - were drawn on the GM's
screen, and on other players' screens, as page markup rather than as text.
A player who knew how could have run their own code in the GM's browser. All
the ways the audit found are closed. Nothing here asks a world to be migrated.

## Fixed

- **Private cards are cleaned before they are shown.** The words of a private
  card travel straight between browsers and never pass the server, which is
  what cleans a normal chat message. They are now cleaned the same way when
  they come from a player, and cards stored before this release are cleaned
  when they are read. The GM's own cards, with their buttons, are unchanged.
- **Names, pictures and item details are escaped** wherever they were printed
  as markup: the name a killer gives a reshaped trace, a character's name in
  incident cards, in the GM panel's "next" line, in the GM's note about an
  Observe with no record and on a camera tile's hover, a tool's name on a
  project or sabotage card, an item's picture, tier and roles on the character
  sheet and in the GM's windows, and the price on a Hope Call card (now taken
  from the GM's own table).
- **Only a GM's message can play a sound for the GMs or ignore the volume
  slider**, except the real safeword card, which any player may still post.
  A player's private card can no longer insist on interrupting a GM's screen
  as a notice; a GM's still can.
- **An evidence or objection card is only shown to the table when its author
  plays the character it speaks as and that character holds the evidence.**
- **A private card with nobody to read it is not posted at all**, instead of
  being posted for everybody. That could only happen in a world with no GM
  user, but it would have made a secret public.
- **Private cards belong to the account that received them**, so a second
  person logging in on the same computer does not see the first one's.
- **The private-card store has limits and says when it is full.** A player's
  card is limited to 32 KB and the player is told when a message is longer,
  messenger threads keep their newest 2000 cards, words of this world's deleted
  messages are removed at start-up (other worlds opened in the same browser are
  left alone), and a GM is told once if the browser can no longer save them.
- A trap that watches an object now names the room where the object was used,
  not the room the trap was built in, and its card title no longer shows
  `&#39;` for an apostrophe.

## Checked

- The headless suite, the eleven scenarios, and new checks: R128 and R129 in
  the suite, and six checks in the security scenario that send hostile markup
  from a player's browser. With the fix taken out, four of them fail.
- An independent review of the stage found a character name printed raw on a
  card the GM's own browser writes, and a start-up tidy that would have
  removed other worlds' private cards from the same browser. Both are fixed
  here, and R129 now also looks for a name handed to a sentence that is
  printed as markup.
- Not checked in a real Foundry yet: that Foundry's own cleaner keeps the
  buttons on a request a player sends to the GM (a Dynamic action, a Hope
  Call). The headless harness checks it against a stand-in for that cleaner.
  Cards written on a GM's own browser are not cleaned, so a GM's ruling cards
  keep their buttons whatever the cleaner does.
